titleEn: Basement Renovation Cost Metro Vancouver 2026: Legal Suite vs. Basic Finish
titleZh: 大温哥华地下室装修费用 2026：合法套房与基础装修指南
contentEn:
A basement renovation in Metro Vancouver in 2026 costs $50,000 at the floor for basic finishing and can exceed $350,000 for a premium legal suite with theatre room and sauna. Most homeowners spending on a permitted, code-compliant conversion fall between $80,000 and $200,000. Those numbers come from real project costs — not estimates — and they vary most by whether the suite is legal (rentable) or informal, and whether the basement has moisture issues.

Reno Stars has completed basement projects across Richmond, Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, and Surrey. This guide covers 2026 pricing, BC Building Code requirements, permit timelines, and what separates a $50K basic finish from a $280K legal secondary suite.

How Much Does a Basement Renovation Cost in Metro Vancouver in 2026?

Metro Vancouver basement costs span a wide range because two identical-looking basements can have radically different underlying conditions. A dry, 7-foot-ceiling, modern-wired basement in a 2010 townhouse is a different project than a damp, 6-foot-ceiling, knob-and-tube-wired basement in a 1940s house. The cost table below reflects projects Reno Stars has completed; all include BC Building Code compliance, fire separation, and written contracts.

ScopeTotal Investment (2026)What's Included
Basic finishing (no kitchen or bath)$50,000 – $90,000Drywall, electrical, lighting, flooring, paint, baseboards; rec room or storage
Finishing + one bathroom$80,000 – $130,000Above + 3-piece bathroom rough-in and finish
Legal secondary suite (1 bedroom)$130,000 – $200,000Full kitchen, 3-piece bath, separate entrance, fire separation, egress windows, separate electrical panel
Legal suite (2 bedroom) + ensuite$180,000 – $280,000Two code-compliant bedrooms, full kitchen, 2 bathrooms, premium finishes throughout
Premium suite + entertainment area$200,000 – $350,000+Wet bar, theatre room, gym, sauna, designer finishes, custom millwork

The $50,000 floor is not arbitrary. Below that price in 2026 Vancouver, a project is cutting one of three things: permits (which voids home insurance and blocks legal rental income), fire separation and egress code compliance (which makes the space illegal to occupy), or contractor insurance (which exposes the homeowner to unlimited liability). Reno Stars includes all three in every basement quote.

What Drives Price Up: The Five Variables

Two basements with the same square footage can differ by $100,000. Here is why, in order of frequency:

1. Ceiling Height — The Single Biggest Variable

BC requires a minimum ceiling height of 6 feet 5 inches under beams for a legal suite. Many Vancouver-area homes built in the 1940s–1960s have 6-foot ceilings or lower. Raising the floor by underpinning the foundation costs $30,000–$80,000 but unlocks the ability to rent the space legally. If the existing ceiling is already 7 feet or more, that cost disappears entirely.

2. Moisture and Waterproofing

A dry basement with no history of damp requires only standard dimple membrane (~$2,000–$5,000). A basement with active seepage or efflorescence requires interior drainage, a sump pump, and possibly exterior excavation. Those fixes add $6,000–$60,000 depending on severity.

3. Electrical: Knob-and-Tube Rewiring

Homes built before 1950 in Vancouver, Burnaby, and New Westminster often still have knob-and-tube wiring. BC Electrical Code requires it be fully replaced before a renovation permit closes. Knob-and-tube rewire adds $10,000–$25,000 to a basement project.

4. Asbestos in Popcorn Ceilings and Pipe Wrap

Any Vancouver-area home built before 1990 may contain asbestos in textured ceiling paint or pipe insulation. BC requires professional abatement before demolition. Asbestos remediation runs $5,000–$25,000 depending on square footage and severity.

5. Separate Electrical Panel and Gas Meter for Legal Suites

A legal secondary suite requires its own BC Hydro account and often its own electrical panel. Utility trenching and panel upgrades add $4,000–$8,000. If the suite has a gas range or gas dryer, FortisBC requires a separate gas meter — another $3,000–$6,000.

What Makes a Basement Suite Legal in BC

BC Building Code Division B, Section 9.36 governs basement suites. A legal secondary suite must meet all of the following before the City will close the permit:

  • Separate entrance — Direct from outside, no shared corridor with the main unit
  • Fire separation — 5/8-inch Type X drywall on the ceiling between units, all penetrations sealed with fire-rated caulk
  • Interconnected smoke and CO alarms — Hardwired throughout both units, per BC Fire Code
  • Egress windows — Each bedroom requires a window with a clear opening of at least 0.35 square metres, minimum 550mm wide, sill height no more than 1 metre above the floor
  • Sound transmission rating STC 50+ — Floor/ceiling assembly between units must achieve STC 50 or better
  • Independent heating — Separate thermostat OR shared system with proper zoning controls
  • Ventilation per BC Section 9.32 — Bathroom and kitchen exhaust directly to exterior
  • Ceiling height — Minimum 6 feet 5 inches under beams for the suite; common areas may be lower

Reno Stars prepares the full permit package including engineered egress window specifications and fire-separation schedules. We coordinate all municipal inspections and do not close a permit until every item passes.

Basement Renovation Timeline in Metro Vancouver

Duration depends on scope and whether the City requires a full permit (legal suites always require one; basic finishing may not):

ScopeDurationPermit Required
Basic finishing (no suite)6–10 weeksMinor permit (not always required)
Finishing + one bathroom8–12 weeksMinor or building permit
Legal 1-bedroom suite12–18 weeksYes — full building permit
Legal 2-bedroom + ensuite16–22 weeksYes — full building permit

Permit processing times in 2026 vary by municipality: City of Vancouver runs 4–8 weeks; Surrey and Burnaby run 3–6 weeks; Richmond and Coquitlam run 3–5 weeks. Those timelines are in addition to construction duration.

Why Choose a Basement Renovation in 2026?

Metro Vancouver's housing shortage has made legal secondary suites one of the highest-ROI renovations available. A 1-bedroom legal suite in Richmond or Burnaby rents for $1,600–$2,200 per month in 2026. At $1,800/month, a legal suite generates $21,600/year in gross rental income — enough to service the interest on a $130,000 renovation loan at today's rates while building long-term equity.

Beyond rental income, a finished basement adds useable square footage without the cost of an addition. It costs $150–$250 per square foot to finish a basement in Metro Vancouver in 2026, compared to $350–$500+ per square foot for an addition with foundation work.

Real Basement Projects by Reno Stars

Every basement project Reno Stars completes starts with a 90-minute in-home assessment: moisture probe, ceiling-height measurement, electrical age evaluation, and a written scope. Quotes include all permit and inspection costs — no hidden fees.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Frequently Asked Questions — Basement Renovation Metro Vancouver

How much does a basement renovation cost in Vancouver in 2026?

A basic basement finishing project in Metro Vancouver costs $50,000–$90,000. A legal secondary suite with separate entrance, kitchen, and bathroom costs $130,000–$200,000. A premium 2-bedroom legal suite with high-end finishes costs $180,000–$280,000. Every price assumes a dry, code-compliant basement with 7-foot ceilings; moisture remediation or underpinning add to the total. Reno Stars has completed basement projects in Richmond, Vancouver, Burnaby, Coquitlam, Surrey, and Delta.

Do I need a permit for a basement renovation in Vancouver?

Yes for any work that includes plumbing, electrical upgrades, structural changes, or creation of a secondary suite. Basic cosmetic finishing (paint, flooring, lighting) may qualify for a minor permit exemption in some municipalities — Reno Stars confirms this during the initial assessment. Any work involving fire separation, egress windows, or a separate entrance always requires a building permit in Metro Vancouver in 2026.

What is required to make a basement suite legal in BC?

A legal secondary suite in BC requires: a separate entrance with direct outdoor access, fire separation between units (5/8-inch Type X drywall on the ceiling), interconnected hardwired smoke and CO alarms, code-compliant egress windows in every bedroom, a sound transmission rating of STC 50 or better in the floor/ceiling assembly, independent ventilation from the main unit, and BC Building Code compliance for ceiling height, bathroom rough-in, and kitchen rough-in. Reno Stars handles all permit applications and coordinates all required municipal inspections.

How long does a basement renovation take in Metro Vancouver?

A basic basement finishing project takes 6–10 weeks. A legal secondary suite with full permit runs 12–18 weeks from permit application to final inspection. Complex 2-bedroom suites with high-end finishes take 16–22 weeks. Permit processing time is separate from construction time and varies by municipality: Vancouver 4–8 weeks, Surrey and Burnaby 3–6 weeks, Richmond and Coquitlam 3–5 weeks in 2026.

Can I do a basement renovation without a legal suite?

Yes. Homeowners who do not want to rent out the space commonly finish the basement as a rec room, home theatre, home gym, or additional bedroom without a kitchen or separate entrance. These projects cost $50,000–$130,000, may not require a full building permit, and can be completed in 6–12 weeks. Reno Stars completes these projects with the same BC Building Code standards, including fire separation, as a legal suite — so the space can be converted to a suite later without redo work.

2026 年，大温哥华地下室装修费用从基本装修的 50,000 加元底线，到配有影院室和桑拿的高级合法套房，最高可超过 350,000 加元。大多数选择合规改造工程的业主，费用在 80,000 至 200,000 加元之间。费用差异主要取决于地下室是否装修成合法（可出租）套房，以及是否存在潮湿问题。

Reno Stars 已在列治文、温哥华、本拿比、高贵林和素里的地下室完成项目。本文涵盖 2026 年定价、BC 建筑规范要求、许可流程，以及 5 万加元基础装修与 28 万加元合法次卧套房的区别。

2026 年大温哥华地下室装修费用是多少？

大温哥华地下室费用差异很大，因为两个看起来相同的地下室可能有截然不同的基础条件。2010 年联排别墅中干燥、7 英尺天花板、现代布线的地下室，与 1940 年代房屋中潮湿、6 英尺天花板、旋钮和管道布线的地下室，是完全不同的工程。下表费用来自 Reno Stars 已完成项目的真实成本，所有项目均包含 BC 建筑规范合规、防火隔离和书面合同。

工程范围2026 年总投资包含内容
基础装修（无厨房或浴室）50,000 – 90,000 加元干墙、电气、照明、地板、油漆、踢脚线；娱乐室或储物间
装修 + 一间浴室80,000 – 130,000 加元上述 + 三件套浴室毛坯和装修
合法次卧套房（一室）130,000 – 200,000 加元设施齐全的厨房、三件套浴室、独立入口、防火隔离、出口窗户、独立电箱
合法套房（两室）+ 套内浴室180,000 – 280,000 加元两间合规卧室、设施齐全的厨房、两间浴室、各处优质装修
高级套房 + 娱乐区200,000 – 350,000 加元以上吧台、影院室、健身房、桑拿房、设计师装修、定制木工

50,000 加元的底线不是任意的。2026 年温哥华地区低于此价格的项目，要么省去了许可证（导致房屋保险失效且无法合法出租），要么省去了防火隔离和出口合规（使空间无法合法居住），要么省去了承包商保险（让业主承担无限责任）。Reno Stars 在每个地下室报价中都包含这三项。

什么推高了价格：五个关键变量

两个面积相同的地下室可能相差 100,000 加元。原因如下，按频率排序：

1. 天花板高度 — 最大单一变量

BC 要求合法套房横梁下方最小净高为 6 英尺 5 英寸。1940 年代至 1960 年代建造的许多温哥华地区房屋净高为 6 英尺或更低。通过地基托换降低地板来增加净高，费用为 30,000 至 80,000 加元，但能解锁合法出租资格。如果现有净高已达 7 英尺或更高，则无此费用。

2. 潮湿与防水

干燥、无潮湿历史的地下室只需标准凹坑板（约 2,000 至 5,000 加元）。而有渗水或风化问题的地下室需要内部排水、污水泵，甚至外部开挖。修复费用根据严重程度额外增加 6,000 至 60,000 加元。

3. 电气：旋钮和管道布线更换

1950 年前建造的温哥华、本拿比和新威斯敏斯特的房屋通常仍使用旋钮和管道布线。BC 电气规范要求在装修许可关闭前完全更换。旋钮和管道更换需额外增加 10,000 至 25,000 加元。

4. 爆米花天花板和管道绝缘中的石棉

1990 年前建造的任何温哥华地区房屋都可能含有纹理的油漆或管道绝缘中的石棉。BC 要求在拆除前进行专业处理。石棉处理费用根据面积和严重程度为 5,000 至 25,000 加元。

5. 合法套房的独立电箱和燃气表

合法次卧套房需要独立的 BC Hydro 账户，通常还需要独立的电箱。公用事业挖掘和电箱升级增加 4,000 至 8,000 加元。如果套房有燃气灶或燃气烘干机，FortisBC 要求独立的燃气表 — 再加 3,000 至 6,000 加元。

什么使 BC 地下室套房合法？

BC 建筑规范 B 分部第 9.36 条管理地下室套房。在市政府关闭许可证之前，合法次卧套房必须满足以下所有条件：

  • 独立入口 — 直接从室外进入，不与主单元共用走廊
  • 防火隔离 — 单元之间天花板使用 5/8 英寸 X 型干墙，所有穿透处用防火密封胶密封
  • 互连烟雾和一氧化碳报警器 — 整个两个单元硬连线，遵从 BC 消防规范
  • 出口窗户 — 每间卧室必须有一扇净开口至少 0.35 平方米、最小宽度 550 毫米、窗台高度不超过地面上方 1 米的窗户
  • 声音传输等级 STC 50+ — 单元之间地板/天花板组件必须达到 STC 50 或以上
  • 独立供暖 — 独立恒温器或带适当分区控制的共享系统
  • 通风（BC 第 9.32 条） — 浴室和厨房排气直接通向室外
  • 净高 — 套房横梁下方最小净高 6 英尺 5 英寸；公共区域可能较低

Reno Stars 准备包括工程出口窗规格和防火隔离时间表在内的完整许可包。我们协调所有市政检查，并在每个项目检查通过后才关闭许可证。

大温哥华地下室装修时间表

工期取决于工程范围，以及市府是否要求完整许可（合法套房始终需要；基础装修可能不需要）：

工程范围工期是否需要许可
基础装修（无套房）6–10 周小许可（并非始终需要）
装修 + 一间浴室8–12 周小许可或建筑许可
合法一室套房12–18 周是 — 完整建筑许可
合法两室 + 套内浴室16–22 周是 — 完整建筑许可

2026 年各市许可证处理时间不同：温哥华市 4–8 周；素里和本拿比 3–6 周；列治文和高贵林 3–5 周。这些时间不计入施工工期。

为什么在 2026 年选择地下室装修？

大温哥华的住房短缺使合法次卧套房成为目前投资回报率最高的装修之一。列治文或本拿比的一室合法套房在 2026 年月租金为 1,600 至 2,200 加元。以每月 1,800 加元计算，合法套房每年产生 21,600 加元的毛租金收入——足以按当前利率为 130,000 加元的装修贷款支付利息，同时积累长期资产净值。

除了租金收入，装修地下室还可以增加可用面积，而无需额外建造费用。2026 年大温哥华地下室装修费用为每平方英尺 150 至 250 加元，而带地基工程的扩建每平方英尺费用为 350 加元以上。

Reno Stars 的真实地下室项目

Reno Stars 完成的每个地下室项目都从 90 分钟入户评估开始：湿度探测、净高测量、电气年龄评估，以及书面范围。报价包含所有许可和检查费用——无隐藏费用。

规划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？获取 Reno Stars 的免费、无义务报价。

常见问题 — 大温哥华地下室装修

2026 年温哥华地下室装修费用是多少？

大温哥华基础地下室装修费用为 50,000 至 90,000 加元。配有独立入口、厨房和浴室的合法次卧套房费用为 130,000 至 200,000 加元。带高档装修的两室合法套房费用为 180,000 至 280,000 加元。每个价格均假设地下室干燥、合规、净高 7 英尺；防潮处理或托换工程会增加总费用。Reno Stars 已在列治文、温哥华、本拿比、高贵林、素里和三角洲完成地下室项目。

温哥华地下室装修需要许可证吗？

涉及管道、电气升级、结构改造或建造次卧套房的工程需要许可证。纯表面装修（油漆、地板、照明）在某些市镇可能符合小许可证豁免条件——Reno Stars 在初步评估期间确认。2026 年大温哥华任何涉及防火隔离、出口窗户或独立入口的工程始终需要建筑许可证。

BC 地下室套房合规需要什么？

BC 合法次卧套房要求：可直接从室外进入的独立入口、单元之间的防火隔离（天花板上使用 5/8 英寸 X 型干墙）、整个两个单元的互连硬连线烟雾和一氧化碳报警器、每间卧室的合规出口窗户、地板/天花板组件声音传输等级达到 STC 50 或以上、独立于主单元的通风系统，以及 BC 建筑规范对净高、浴室毛坯和厨房毛坯的要求。Reno Stars 处理所有许可申请并协调所有必需的市政检查。

大温哥华地下室装修需要多长时间？

基础地下室装修需要 6–10 周。带完整许可的合法次卧套房从申请许可到最终检查需要 12–18 周。带高档装修的两室复杂套房需要 16–22 周。许可处理时间不计入施工时间，各市时间不同：2026 年温哥华 4–8 周，素里和本拿比 3–6 周，列治文和高贵林 3–5 周。

我可以不建合法套房就做地下室装修吗？

可以。不想出租空间的业主通常将地下室装修成娱乐室、家庭影院、家庭健身房或额外卧室，不需要厨房或独立入口。这些项目费用为 50,000 至 130,000 加元，可能不需要完整建筑许可证，可在 6–12 周内完成。Reno Stars 以与合法套房相同的 BC 建筑规范标准完成这些项目，包括防火隔离——因此空间日后可随时转换为套房，无需返工。
